newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Debut deals sealed.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Debut deals sealed.

text.p: Debut deals grabbed the headlines in Asian debt markets on Wednesday.
Japan's Toyota Motor Credit Corp (TMCC) launched the first ever mark-denominated Euro-Asian bond, a one billion mark issue launched via lead managers Merrill Lynch and SBC Warburg.
The five-year AAA-rated bonds priced to yield five basis points over comparable German government bunds, on the tight end of the indicated 5-7 basis point range.
The bonds will be listed in Frankfurt, Hong Kong, London and Singapore.
"Euro-Asian" bonds are listed on European and Asian exchanges and are marketed in both regions.
Demand for fixed-rate paper in Asia typically comes from central banks, some institutional funds and banks trading for their own accounts.

In Hong Kong, Dah Sing Bank launched a HK$1.2 billion floating rate certificate of deposit issue. The three-year paper pays a margin of 40 basis points over the three-month Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate and, with fees, an all-in return of 56 basis points to top tier participants.
Application will be made to the Hong Kong Monetary Authority to accept the certificates as eligible for its Liquidity Adjustment Facility, or discount window.
Eligibility for LAF makes an issue more attractive to banks because holders of the qualifying debt can engage in repurchase agreements with the monetary authority, increasing liquidity.
If accepted, the issue will be the first LAF-eligible deal for Dah Sing, which was assigned an A-minus rating by European rating agency IBCA in September.
China Development Finance Co (HK), Commerz (East Asia, HSBC Markets, United Overseas Bank and Westpac Banking Corp are arrangers.
Bank of East Asia is set to launch its HK$1.8 billion FRCD issue on Thursday, which also is expected to be LAF-eligible.
The three-year paper is expected to pay an all-in return of 41 to 44 basis points.
The deal is no first, however. In February, Bank of East Asia completed a HK$2 billion three-year LAF FRCD that paid 48 basis points all-in.
Arrangers are China Development Finance Co (HK), Societe Generale Asia, Sumitomo Finance Asia, Bayerische Landesbank Hongkong, Westpac Banking Corp and UBS Hong Kong.

And in another first, the first-ever perpetual bond for an Asian issuer is expected to be launched on Thursday. The subordinated undated bond will be launched for a unit of Hong Kong's Swire Pacific via Merrill Lynch.
